answer: When a large generator trips, grid frequency dips everywhere on that interconnection, so a device proves its grid by reporting the dip depth and recovery shape, and readings from nearby devices must agree on the same event. An onyx dark control room sees the same second everywhere, and no fable of a calm grid survives, because every real device felt the same dip; a copied reading fails for a second identity, and a velvet cover over one device's reading cannot hide that the verifier also demands the device's own local noise.
